   115	/// Reports are advisory: compatibility cannot license calls or prove unchanged behavior.
   116	pub fn compare(old: &Bound, new: &Bound, label: &str) -> Vec<String> {
   117	    let mut lines=Vec::new();
   118	    for before in old.programs.iter().filter(|p|p.program.kind!=ProgramKind::Job) {
   119	        let name=&before.program.name;
   120	        let prefix=format!("old-client compatibility ({label}), operation {name}");
   121	        let Some(after)=new.programs.iter().find(|p|p.program.name==*name) else {
   122	            lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: removed operation; old calls get E_OP; keep `alias {name} = replacement` for a same-module query/mutation, or retain a wrapper"));continue;
   123	        };
   124	        if before.program.kind!=after.program.kind {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: operation kind changed; retain the old endpoint kind"));continue;}
   125	        let rename_candidate = |new_kind: &A| before.program.args.iter().find(|(old_name, old_kind)|
   126	            !after.program.args.contains_key(*old_name) && !after.program.arg_aliases.contains_key(*old_name)
   127	                && accepts_in(old_kind,new_kind,Some(old),Some(new)));
   128	        let mut warned_renames=BTreeSet::new();
   129	        for (arg,kind) in &after.program.args {
   130	            if before.program.args.contains_key(arg) { continue; }
   131	            if let Some((old_arg,old_kind))=before.program.args.iter().find(|(old,_)|after.program.arg_aliases.get(*old)==Some(arg)) {
   132	                if !accepts_in(old_kind,kind,Some(old),Some(new)) {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: aliased argument {old_arg} → {arg} narrows the old input domain ({old_kind:?} → {kind:?}); retain the old input domain or a compatible wrapper"));}
   133	            } else if !matches!(kind,A::Optional(_)) {
   134	                if let Some((old,_))=rename_candidate(kind) {
   135	                    lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: required argument {old} appears renamed to {arg}; old calls get E_INPUT; declare `{arg}: <new type> alias {old}` if it is the same value, or retain a compatible wrapper"));
   136	                    warned_renames.insert(old.clone());
   137	                } else {
   138	                    lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: clients calling without new required argument {arg} get E_INPUT; give {arg} a fitting `default <literal>` or retain a compatible wrapper"));
   139	                }
   140	            }
   141	        }
   142	        for (arg,kind) in &before.program.args {
   143	            match after.program.args.get(arg) {
   144	                None if after.program.arg_aliases.contains_key(arg)=>{
   145	                    let next=&after.program.args[&after.program.arg_aliases[arg]];

   151	                _=>{}

   160	                _=>{}
   161	            }
   162	        }

   166	                let target=after.program.args.contains_key(spelling).then_some(spelling).or_else(||after.program.arg_aliases.get(spelling));

   169	                        lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: independent arguments {prior} and {canonical} now share {target}; old calls containing both positions get E_INPUT; retain separate arguments or a compatible wrapper"));
   170	                    }
   171	                }
   172	            }
   173	        }

   180	            }
   181	        }

   183	        let typed_change=result_change(&before.result,&after.result,old,new);
   184	        let change=combine([action_change,typed_change],false);
   185	        match change {
   186	            ResultChange::Additive=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT NOTE: result shape added fields while preserving prior fields and domains; old clients may ignore the additions")),
   187	            ResultChange::Changed=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT REVIEW: result shape/value domain changed; preserve the old projection/domain or introduce a new operation before retiring old clients")),
   188	            ResultChange::Same=>{},
   189	        }
   190	        let old_domains=crate::result_domains::signature(before,old);
   191	        let new_domains=crate::result_domains::signature(after,new);
   192	        // A domain introduced only for a newly returned field is covered by
   193	        // the additive result note. Existing or removed domains still need review.
   194	        let changed:Vec<_>=old_domains.keys().collect::<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>>().into_iter().filter(|key|old_domains.get(*key)!=new_domains.get(*key)).cloned().collect();

   196	        if refusals(before)!=refusals(after) {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: BEHAVIOR REVIEW: refusal codes/messages changed ({:?} → {:?}); verify intended denials separately from input breaks",refusals(before),refusals(after)));}
   197	    }
   198	    lines
   199	}

   202	pub fn compact(lines:&[String])->Vec<String>{

   204	    let mut out=Vec::new();let mut groups=BTreeMap::<String,BTreeSet<String>>::new();

   210	        }else{groups.entry(detail.into()).or_default().insert(operation.into());}
   211	    }
   212	    for(detail,ops)in groups{out.push(format!("old-client compatibility: RESULT REVIEW: {detail}; operations [{}]; verify old-client handling (full per-operation evidence in --json)",ops.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")));}
   213	    out
   214	}

    26	pub fn duration(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    27	    if text.starts_with('-') { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
    28	    let text = text.strip_prefix('+').unwrap_or(text);
    29	    let split = text.bytes().position(|b| !b.is_ascii_digit()).unwrap_or(text.len());
    30	    let (number, unit) = text.split_at(split);
    31	    let multiplier = match unit { "ms" => 1, "s" => 1_000, "m" => 60_000, "h" => 3_600_000, "d" => 86_400_000, "w" => 604_800_000, _ => 0 };
    32	    number.parse::<i64>().ok().and_then(|n| n.checked_mul(multiplier)).filter(|n| *n > 0 && *n <= MAX_TIME)
    33	        .ok_or_else(|| input("expected a positive whole duration with ms, s, m, h, d or w, such as +25h"))
    34	}

    65	impl Clock {
    66	    pub fn new(dev: bool, offset: i64) -> Result<Self, Refusal> {
    67	        if !dev && offset != 0 { return Err(release()); }
    68	        Ok(Self { dev, offset, base: time(snapback4_core::now_ms().checked_add(offset))?, started: Instant::now(),

    70	    }
    71	    pub fn staging(offset: i64, floor: i64) -> Result<Self, Refusal> {
    72	        let mut clock = Self::new(true, offset)?;
    73	        let delta = floor.saturating_sub(clock.now()).max(0);
    74	        if delta > 0 { clock.advance(delta)?; }
    75	        Ok(clock)
    76	    }

    78	    pub(crate) fn freeze(&mut self, now: i64) { self.base = now; self.frozen = true; }
    79	    pub fn now(&self) -> i64 {
    80	        #[cfg(test)] if self.frozen { return self.base; }
    81	        if !self.dev { return snapback4_core::now_ms(); }
    82	        self.base.saturating_add(self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64).min(MAX_TIME)
    83	    }

    87	    pub fn presence_now(&self) -> i64 {

    98	        self.started = Instant::now();
    99	        #[cfg(test)] { self.frozen = false; }
   100	        Ok(self.base)
   101	    }
   102	    pub fn advance(&mut self, milliseconds: i64) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
   103	        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
   104	        if milliseconds <= 0 { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
   105	        let next = time(self.now().checked_add(milliseconds))?;
   106	        let offset = self.offset.checked_add(milliseconds).ok_or_else(|| input("cumulative clock offset overflow"))?;
   107	        self.revision += 1;
   108	        self.offset = offset;
   109	        self.base = next;
   110	        self.started = Instant::now();
   111	        Ok(next)
   112	    }
   113	}
   114	
   115	/// The control CLI only talks to a loopback dev host. It does not open its store.
   116	pub fn command(options: &crate::verbs::Options) -> i32 {
   117	    let result = (|| -> Result<String, String> {
   118	        let draining = options.positionals == ["drain"];
   119	        if !draining && (options.positionals.len() != 2 || options.positionals[0] != "advance") {
   120	            return Err(input(format!("usage: {}", crate::cli_flags::synopsis("clock"))).to_string());
   121	        }
   122	        let duration_text = if draining { "0ms" } else { options.positionals[1].as_str() };
   123	        if !draining { duration(duration_text).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?; }
   124	        let release_path = options.flags.get("release").map(|dir| std::path::PathBuf::from(dir).join("store.sqlite"));
   125	        if release_path.is_some() && options.flags.contains_key("port") { return Err("clock --release does not accept --port".into()); }
   126	        let (address, instance, token) = if let Some(path) = &release_path {
   127	            let store = snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::open_read_only(path).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
   128	            if store.deployment_environment().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?.as_deref() != Some("staging") { return Err(release().to_string()); }
   129	            let address = crate::store_owner::inspector_address(path).ok_or("staging clock requires a running serve")?;
   130	            let session = crate::serve::token::mint_live(path, "clock", 1).map_err(|(_,error)|error)?;
   131	            (address,None,Some(session.token))
   132	        } else {
   133	            let (address,instance)=crate::verbs::dev_address(options)?;
   134	            // A production listener has no development-token registry entry.
   135	            // Ask its read-only clock door first so the CLI preserves the
   136	            // server's actionable refusal instead of failing token discovery.
   137	            if let Ok((_, status)) = crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange(address, "GET", "/dev/clock/status", None, "", Duration::from_secs(5))
   138	                && status["denied"]["code"] == "E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY"
   139	            {
   140	                return Err(release().to_string());
   141	            }
   142	            let token=crate::verbs::mint_for_dev(address,"operator",1)?;
   143	            (address,instance,Some(token))
   144	        };
   145	        let mut body = serde_json::json!({"duration":duration_text,"eachBoundary":options.flags.contains_key("each-boundary"), "drain":!options.flags.contains_key("no-drain"), "allowHeld":options.flags.contains_key("allow-held")});
   146	        if options.flags.contains_key("expire-sessions") { body["sessions"] = "expire".into(); }
   147	        if draining && options.flags.contains_key("no-drain") { return Err(input("clock drain does not accept --no-drain").to_string()); }
   148	        let body = body.to_string();
   149	        // The common HTTP/1.0 exchange is EOF-delimited and bounds replies at
   150	        // 64 MiB, enough for the preflight's complete explicit window report.
   151	        let response = if release_path.is_some() {
   152	            crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_authorized(address,"POST","/dev/clock/advance",None,token.as_deref(),&body,Duration::from_secs(60))
   153	        } else {
   154	            crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_dev_authorized(address,"/dev/clock/advance",instance.as_deref(),token.as_deref().unwrap(),&body,Duration::from_secs(60))
   155	        };
   156	        let (status, json) = response.map_err(|error| {
   157	            let evidence = crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange(address, "GET", "/dev/status", None, "", Duration::from_secs(5)).ok()
   158	                .map(|(_, status)| format!("now={}, skewMs={}", status["now"], status["skewMs"]))
   159	                .unwrap_or_else(|| "clock status unavailable".into());
   160	            format!("clock advance reply failed at {address}: {error}; time may already have advanced ({evidence}); inspect /dev/status and queued work before retrying; for an isolated dev pass --port N")
   161	        })?;
   162	        if let Some(notice) = json["sessionNotice"].as_str() { eprintln!("clock: {notice}"); }
   163	        if let Some(held) = json["held"].as_array() {
   164	            for schedule in held.iter().filter(|s| s["holdCode"] == "saved-boundary") {
   165	                eprintln!("clock: schedule {}: {}", schedule["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("?"), schedule["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or("held"));
   166	            }
   167	        }
   168	        if let Some(denied) = json.get("denied") {
   169	            if json.get("now").is_some() {
   170	                eprintln!("clock: incomplete advance report (time already moved): {}", serde_json::json!({"now":json["now"],"fired":json["fired"],"held":json["held"]}));
   171	            }
   172	            let clock = json["message"].as_str().map(|message| format!("; time remains advanced: {message}")).unwrap_or_default();
   173	            return Err(format!("{}: {}{clock}\n  guide: clock", denied["code"].as_str().unwrap_or("E_CLOCK_INPUT"), denied["message"].as_str().unwrap_or("clock advance failed")));
   174	        }
   175	        if status != 200 { return Err(format!("dev refused clock advance: {json}")); }
   176	        Ok(json.to_string())
   177	    })();
   178	    match result { Ok(body) => { println!("{body}"); 0 }, Err(error) => { eprintln!("{error}"); 1 } }
   179	}

    66	/// `/seed` rows checked against the served schema and typed, or the first problem.
    67	fn typed_rows(schema: &snapback4_core::Schema, rows: &[Json], now: i64) -> Result<Vec<(String, snapback4_core::Value)>, Refusal> {
    68	    let mut typed = Vec::new();
    69	    for (index, entry) in rows.iter().enumerate() {
    70	        let (Some(table), Some(row)) = (entry.get("table").and_then(Json::as_str), entry.get("row")) else {
    71	            return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", "each seed entry is {table, row}"));
    72	        };
    73	        let Some(definition) = schema.table(table) else {
    74	            return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("unknown table {table}")));
    75	        };
    76	        if row.is_object() && row.get("id").is_none_or(|id| !id.is_string()) {
    77	            return Err(missing_id(index, table));
    78	        }
    79	        let mut row = row.clone();
    80	        crate::verbs::test_fixture::relative_times(definition, &mut row, now)
    81	            .map_err(|why| Refusal::new("E_FIXTURE_TIME", "input", format!("seed row {index} ({table}): {why}")))?;
    82	        if let Some(why) = wire::bare_principal(definition, &row) {
    83	            return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("seed row {index} ({table}): {why}")));
    84	        }
    85	        match wire::row_from_json(definition, &row) {
    86	            Ok(value) => typed.push((table.to_owned(), value)),
    87	            Err(why) => return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("{table}: {why}"))),
    88	        }
    89	    }
    90	    Ok(typed)
    91	}

    93	fn seed_refusal(error: snapback4_core::RuntimeError) -> Refusal {
    94	    let mut refusal = error.refusal();
    95	    // Reseeding with changed immutable values reads like a rule problem; say what happened.
    96	    if refusal.code == "E_CONSTRAINT" && refusal.message.ends_with(" is immutable") {
    97	        refusal.message.push_str("; /seed is an upsert by id, and a row with that id already exists with a different value in that column. Reseed it with its original value, give the row a new id, POST /dev/reset first, or restart dev with --memory for an empty store");
    98	    }
    99	    refusal
   100	}

   102	/// What `POST /dev/reset` was asked to do: the body is empty, a `/seed`
   103	/// array, or `{"seed": [..], "clock": "reset"}` with either key optional.
   104	#[derive(Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
   105	struct ResetRequest { seed: Vec<Json>, clock: bool }
   106	
   107	fn reset_request(body: &str) -> Result<ResetRequest, Refusal> {
   108	    const SHAPE: &str = "reset takes no body, a /seed array [{table, row}, ..], or {\"seed\": [..], \"clock\": \"reset\"} with either key optional";
   109	    if body.trim().is_empty() { return Ok(ResetRequest::default()); }
   110	    match serde_json::from_str(body) {
   111	        Ok(Json::Array(seed)) => Ok(ResetRequest { seed, clock: false }),
   112	        Ok(Json::Object(fields)) => {
   113	            let mut request = ResetRequest::default();
   114	            for (key, value) in fields {
   115	                match (key.as_str(), value) {
   116	                    ("seed", Json::Array(seed)) => request.seed = seed,
   117	                    ("clock", Json::String(clock)) if clock == "reset" => request.clock = true,
   118	                    ("clock", Json::String(clock)) if clock == "keep" => request.clock = false,
   119	                    ("clock", other) => return Err(crate::dev_clock::input(format!("reset's clock is \"reset\" (back to wall time) or \"keep\" (the default), not {other}"))),
   120	                    (key, _) => return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("{SHAPE}; got key {key:?}"))),
   121	                }
   122	            }
   123	            Ok(request)
   124	        }
   125	        _ => Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", SHAPE)),
   126	    }
   127	}

   687	pub(super) fn clock_status(request: Request, shared: &Shared) {
   688	    if let Err(why) = clock_service(&request, shared) { return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&why)})); }
   689	    let result = (|| {
   690	        let (epoch, reader) = shared.reader()?;
   691	        let note = crate::dev_clock_store::ahead(&reader, shared.now());
   692	        lock(&shared.readers).put(&epoch, reader.into_inner());
   693	        note
   694	    })();
   695	    match result {
   696	        Ok(note) => { let now = shared.now(); respond(request, 200, json!({"storeAhead":note,"now":now,"skewMs":now - snapback4_core::now_ms()})) },
   697	        Err(error) => respond(request, refusal_status(&error.refusal(), 500), json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error.refusal())})),
   698	    }
   699	}

    24	        {
    25	            if let Some(value) = principal(value) {
    26	                seats.insert(value.into());
    27	            }
    28	        }
    29	        RuleExpr::And(rules) | RuleExpr::Or(rules) => rules
    30	            .iter()
    31	            .for_each(|rule| self::rule(rule, seats, positive)),
    32	        RuleExpr::Not(rule) => self::rule(rule, seats, !positive),
    33	        _ => {}
    34	    }
    35	}
    36	
    37	fn expression(expr: &Expr, seats: &mut BTreeSet<String>, positive: bool) {
    38	    match expr {
    39	        Expr::Binary {
    40	            op: BinaryOp::Eq | BinaryOp::SameValueZero,
    41	            left,
    42	            right,
    43	        } => match (&**left, &**right, positive) {
    44	            (Expr::Input(Input::Viewer), Expr::Literal(value), true)
    45	            | (Expr::Literal(value), Expr::Input(Input::Viewer), true) => {
    46	                if let Some(value) = principal(value) {
    47	                    seats.insert(value.into());
    48	                }
    49	            }
    50	            _ => {}
    51	        },
    52	        Expr::Binary {
    53	            op: BinaryOp::And | BinaryOp::Or,
    54	            left,
    55	            right,
    56	        } => {
    57	            expression(left, seats, positive);
    58	            expression(right, seats, positive);
    59	        }
    60	        Expr::Unary {
    61	            op: snapback4_core::ir::UnaryOp::Not,
    62	            value,
    63	        } => expression(value, seats, !positive),
    64	        Expr::Block { body, value } => {
    65	            statements(body, seats);
    66	            expression(value, seats, positive);
    67	        }
    68	        _ => {}
    69	    }
    70	}
    71	
    72	fn statements(body: &[Stmt], seats: &mut BTreeSet<String>) {
    73	    for statement in body {
    74	        match statement {
    75	            Stmt::Require { condition, .. } => expression(condition, seats, true),
    76	            Stmt::If {
    77	                then_body,
    78	                else_body,
    79	                ..
    80	            } => {
    81	                statements(then_body, seats);
    82	                statements(else_body, seats);
    83	            }
    84	            Stmt::For { body, .. } => statements(body, seats),
    85	            Stmt::Check { condition, .. } => expression(condition, seats, true),
    86	            Stmt::WriteTarget {
    87	                condition: Some(condition),
    88	                ..
    89	            } => statements(&condition.setup, seats),
    90	            _ => {}
    91	        }
    92	    }
    93	}
    94	
    95	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — minted seats stay ordinary principals; this is advisory schema evidence, never a grant.
    96	pub(crate) fn collect(bound: &snapback4_lang::Bound) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    97	    let mut seats = BTreeSet::new();
    98	    for table in bound.schema.tables.values() {
    99	        for rule in [
   100	            &table.rules.read,
   101	            &table.rules.insert,
   102	            &table.rules.update,
   103	            &table.rules.delete,
   104	        ] {
   105	            self::rule(rule, &mut seats, true);
   106	        }
   107	        for rule in table.column_reads.values() {
   108	            self::rule(rule, &mut seats, true);
   109	        }
   110	    }
   111	    for program in &bound.programs {
   112	        statements(&program.program.body, &mut seats);
   113	    }
   114	    seats.extend(
   115	        bound
   116	            .schema
   117	            .schedules
   118	            .iter()
   119	            .filter_map(|schedule| schedule.service.clone()),
   120	    );
   121	    seats.extend(
   122	        bound
   123	            .schema
   124	            .routes
   125	            .values()
   126	            .filter_map(|route| route.service.clone()),
   127	    );
   128	    seats
   129	}

   136	  const host = await nativeHost("serve", [directory], { ...opts, args: [...(opts.args ?? []), ...(opts.clockOffset === undefined ? [] : ["--clock-offset", opts.clockOffset])] });
   137	  const clockCall = async (body?: object): Promise<ClockAdvance> => {
   138	    const config = await fetchIdentity(`${host.url}/auth/config`, deadline(opts.timeoutMs, 10_000));
   139	    if (!config.response.ok || config.body.environment !== "staging") throw Error("E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY: clock controls require a deploy --staging store");
   140	    const clockToken = served.operatorToken("clock");
   141	    const response = await fetch(`${host.url}/dev/clock/${body ? "advance" : "status"}`, { method: body ? "POST" : "GET", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${await clockToken}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, ...(body ? { body: JSON.stringify(body) } : {}), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(deadline(opts.timeoutMs, 60_000)) });
   142	    const result = await response.json() as Partial<ClockAdvance> & { sessionNotice?: string; denied?: { code?: string; message?: string } };
   143	    if (result.sessionNotice) process.stderr.write(`snapback4: ${result.sessionNotice}\n`);
   144	    if (!response.ok || result.denied || !Number.isSafeInteger(result.now)) throw Object.assign(Error(`staging clock refused or reply unavailable; inspect clock and queued work before retrying: ${result.denied?.code ?? response.status} ${result.denied?.message ?? ""}`), { report: result });
   145	    if (body && (!Array.isArray(result.fired) || !Array.isArray(result.held))) throw Error("staging clock reply has no schedule report; inspect clock and queued work before retrying");
   146	    for (const schedule of result.held ?? []) if (schedule.holdCode === "saved-boundary") process.stderr.write(`snapback4: schedule ${schedule.name}: ${schedule.reason}\n`);
   147	    const report: ClockAdvance = { now: result.now!, fired: result.fired ?? [], held: result.held ?? [], maintenancePaused: result.maintenancePaused ?? false, valueOf() { return this.now; } };
   148	    return report;
   149	  };
   150	  // Exit can precede inherited watchdog flock release. The private local
   151	  // barrier observes the same canonical ownership sidecar without writing data.
   152	  let stopping: Promise<void> | undefined;
   153	  const stop = () => stopping ??= (async () => {
   154	    await host.stop();
   155	    const result = await cli(["serve", directory, "--wait-stopped"], {...opts, timeoutMs:6000});
   156	    if (result.code !== 0) throw Error(`proof serve store release failed: ${result.stderr}`);
   157	  })().catch(error => { stopping = undefined; throw error; });
   158	  const served: ServeHost = { ...host, stop,
   159	    now: async () => (await clockCall()).now,
   160	    advance: (duration, options = {}) => {
   161	      if (typeof duration !== "string" || (!/^\+?\d+(ms|s|m|h|d|w)$/.test(duration) || BigInt(duration.replace(/\D/g, "")) === 0n)) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: advance requires a positive whole duration");
   162	      return clockCall({ duration, ...options });
   163	    },
   164	    drain: (options = {}) => clockCall({ duration: "0ms", drain: true, ...options }),
   165	    operatorToken: async (service = "operator", days = 1) => {
   166	      if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(service) || !Number.isSafeInteger(days) || days < 1 || days > 3650) throw Error("proof operatorToken: invalid service or days (1..3650)");
   167	      const result = await cli(["token", "--service", service, "--days", String(days), "--release", directory, "--quiet"], opts);
   168	      if (result.code !== 0) throw Error(`proof operator token refused: ${result.stderr}`);
   169	      const token = result.stdout.trim();
   170	      if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/.test(token)) throw Error("proof operator token malformed");
   171	      return token;
   172	    },
   173	    seedAccounts: accountOptions => seedAccounts(served, accountOptions),
   174	    provisionAccounts: accountOptions => provisionAccounts(served, accountOptions),
   175	  };
   176	  try {
   177	    if (opts.seedUsers && opts.provisionUsers) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: choose seedUsers for staging or provisionUsers for production");
   178	    if (opts.seedUsers) served.sessions = await served.seedAccounts(opts.seedUsers);
   179	    if (opts.provisionUsers) served.sessions = await served.provisionAccounts(opts.provisionUsers);
   180	    return served;
   181	  }
   182	  catch (error) { await served.stop(); throw error; }
   183	}
   210	export interface CliResult { code: number | null; signal: NodeJS.Signals | null; stdout: string; stderr: string; logs: ProofHost["logs"] }
   211	/** Waits for close (stdio drained), never merges the two streams. Nonzero is returned for refusal assertions. */
   212	/** @throws spawn error or command deadline; nonzero exit is returned in code, not thrown. */
   213	export function cli(args: readonly string[], options: ProofOptions = {}): Promise<CliResult> {
   214	  return command(process.execPath, [fileURLToPath(new URL("../bin/snapback4.js", import.meta.url)), ...args], { ...options, secret: options.secret || args[0] === "token" });
   215	}
   216	/** A bounded directly spawned build/tool command, with the same file logs. */
   217	/** @throws spawn error or command deadline; nonzero exit is returned in code, not thrown. */
   218	export async function command(binary: string, args: readonly string[], options: ProofOptions = {}): Promise<CliResult> {
   219	  const run = logged(binary, args, { ...options, processGroup: true, env: { ...process.env, ...options.env } });
   220	  try {
   221	    await bounded(run.closed, deadline(options.timeoutMs, 120_000), "proof cli close");
   222	    if (run.error()) throw run.error();
   223	    return { code: run.code(), signal: run.signal(), stdout: run.stdout(), stderr: logText(run.logs.stderr), logs: run.logs };
   224	  } catch (error) { await stopChild(run.child, deadline(options.stopTimeoutMs, 5000)); throw error; }
   225	  finally { run.child.stdout?.destroy(); } // Secret capture must not pin the driver after a deadline.
   226	}
   227	async function successful(args: string[], options: ProofOptions) {
   228	  const result = await cli(args, options);
   229	  if (result.code !== 0) {
   230	    const stdout = result.stdout.trimEnd();
   231	    const tail = stdout.length > 4000 ? `…${stdout.slice(-4000)}` : stdout;
   232	    throw Error(`proof CLI failed (${result.code}): ${result.stderr}; stdout tail: ${tail || "(empty)"}; logs: ${result.logs.stderr}`);
   233	  }
   234	  return result;
   235	}
   337	const substringLocators = new WeakMap<Locator, { locator: Locator; scoped: boolean }>();
   338	/** Match the smallest visible element whose composed descendant text matches.
   339	 * Strings normalize whitespace and stay exact by default; regexes keep their
   340	 * own semantics. Editable values never count. Independent matches remain
   341	 * ambiguous, including repeated rows. */
   342	/** @throws None at construction; locator observation can refuse ambiguous or invalid selectors. */
   343	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#11-wave-22-loop-repairs-dx6 — composed text preserves exactness and ambiguity.
   344	export function renderedText(page: Page, text: string | RegExp, options: { within?: Locator; exact?: boolean } | null = {}): Locator {
   345	  const normalized = options ?? {};
   346	  const root = normalized.within ?? page;
   347	  const match = (exact: boolean) => registeredLocator(root.locator(`${renderedSelector}=${JSON.stringify({
   348	    source: typeof text === "string" ? text : text.source,
   349	    flags: typeof text === "string" ? "" : text.flags,
   350	    regex: typeof text !== "string", exact,
   351	  })}`));
   352	  const locator = match(normalized.exact ?? true);
   353	  if (typeof text === "string" && normalized.exact !== false) substringLocators.set(locator, { locator: match(false), scoped: normalized.within !== undefined });
   354	  return locator;
   355	}

   357	export interface ExhaustPagesOptions {
   358	  /** Refuse rather than loop forever when a backend returns bad continuations. */
   359	  maxPages?: number;
   360	  /** Names the read in a refusal without exposing its rows or cursor. */
   361	  label?: string;
   362	}
   363	type ProofPage<Row> =
   364	  | { readonly data: readonly Row[]; readonly next?: Cursor | null; readonly complete: boolean; readonly cut: ReadCut; readonly existence?: "present" | "absent" | "partial" }
   365	  | { readonly denied: Refusal }
   366	  | { readonly loading: true };
   367	/** Read every page by passing each opaque `next` back unchanged. The callback
   368	 * receives null first. Refusals, loading, malformed/repeated cursors and a
   369	 * capped or incomplete page fail instead of returning a partial snapshot. */
   370	/** @throws E_PROOF_PAGE for a refused, loading, malformed, repeated, incomplete or over-limit traversal; callback errors propagate. */
   371	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — proof traversal must never promote capped or partial reads to complete evidence.
   372	export async function exhaustPages<Row>(readPage: (cursor: Cursor | null) => Promise<ProofPage<Row>>, options: ExhaustPagesOptions = {}): Promise<Row[]> {
   373	  const maxPages = options.maxPages ?? 1_000, label = options.label ?? "paged read";
   374	  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(maxPages) || maxPages < 1) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: maxPages must be a positive safe integer`);
   375	  const rows: Row[] = [], seen = new Set<string>();
   376	  let cursor: Cursor | null = null;
   377	  for (let pageNumber = 1; pageNumber <= maxPages; pageNumber++) {
   378	    const page = await readPage(cursor);
   379	    if (!page || typeof page !== "object") throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned no read envelope`);
   380	    if ("denied" in page) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} refused ${page.denied.code}: ${page.denied.message}`);
   381	    if ("loading" in page) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is still loading`);
   382	    if (!Array.isArray(page.data)) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} data is not an array`);
   383	    if (page.cut !== null) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is incomplete (${page.cut === undefined ? "missing" : page.cut} cut)`);
   384	    if (page.complete !== true) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is incomplete (complete must be true)`);
   385	    if (page.existence === "partial") throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} has partial existence`);
   386	    rows.push(...page.data);
   387	    const next = page.next ?? null;
   388	    if (next === null) return rows;
   389	    if (typeof next !== "string" || next.length === 0) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned a malformed cursor`);
   390	    if (seen.has(next)) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned a repeated cursor`);
   391	    seen.add(next);
   392	    cursor = next as Cursor;
   393	  }
   394	  throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: exceeded maxPages ${maxPages}`);
   395	}
   396	/** Activate before taking a screenshot, particularly on loaded shared hosts. */
   397	/** @throws page closed or browser activation failed. */
   398	export async function frontPage(page: Page): Promise<Page> { await page.bringToFront(); return page; }

     4	/** Authenticated development and staging return this exact bearer's current live lifetime.
     5	 * Matching the dispatch bearer is the caller's responsibility. Same-bearer
     6	 * preservation is monotonic, so a delayed old reply cannot undo a jump. */
     7	export function reconciledTiming(session: Session, response: Response): Session {
     8	  if (response.headers.get("x-snapback-session-timing") !== "staging") return session;
     9	  const expiry = Number(response.headers.get("x-snapback-session-expires"));
    10	  const capText = response.headers.get("x-snapback-session-cap");
    11	  const cap = capText === null ? undefined : Number(capText);
    12	  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(expiry) || expiry <= 0) return session;
    13	  const read = isReadToken(session.token);
    14	  if (read && (cap === undefined || !Number.isSafeInteger(cap) || cap < expiry)) return session;
    15	  if (!read && cap !== undefined) return session;
    16	  const expiresAt = Math.max(session.expiresAt, expiry);
    17	  const capExpiresAt = cap === undefined ? undefined : Math.max(session.capExpiresAt ?? 0, cap);
    18	  if (expiresAt === session.expiresAt && capExpiresAt === session.capExpiresAt) return session;
    19	  return { ...session, expiresAt, ...(capExpiresAt === undefined ? {} : { capExpiresAt }) };
    20	}

    26	/** Expired local metadata may be superseded by a preserving development or staging jump.
    27	 * Read-only probing creates no session and never widens or refreshes one. */
    28	export async function restoreStagingTiming(base: string, session: Session, fetcher: typeof fetch): Promise<Session | null> {
    29	  const aborter = new AbortController();
    30	  const timer = setTimeout(() => aborter.abort(), 10_000);
    31	  (timer as { unref?: () => void }).unref?.();
    32	  try {
    33	    const response = await fetcher(`${base}/probe?scope=1`, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${session.token}` }, signal: aborter.signal });
    34	    if (!response.ok) return null;
    35	    const next = reconciledTiming(session, response);
    36	    const stamp = Number(response.headers.get("x-snapback-time"));
    37	    if (next === session || !Number.isSafeInteger(stamp) || next.expiresAt <= stamp) return null;
    38	    // Consume the bounded ordinary probe body before blessing restoration.
    39	    const { readResponse } = await import("./http-response.ts");
    40	    const body = await readResponse(response);
    41	    return body.ok === true && body.viewer === session.principal && body.scope === (isReadToken(session.token) ? "read" : "full") ? next : null;
    42	  } catch { return null; }
    43	  finally { clearTimeout(timer); }
    44	}

   124	/// Population advice only for a newly declared/changed window, before adoption.
   125	// @ref LLP 3000.007#8 — bounded catalog probes never adopt or acquire a writer lock.
   126	pub(super) fn window_populations(path: &Path, candidate: &Schema) -> Result<Vec<(String, u32, u64)>> {
   127	    if !candidate.visible_tables().any(|(_, table)| table.ephemeral.is_none() && table.sync.as_ref().is_some_and(|s| s.horizon.is_some())) { return Ok(Vec::new()); }

   129	    conn.begin_snapshot()?;
   130	    let adopted = conn.inspection_adopted()?;
   131	    if !adopted { return Ok(Vec::new()); }
   132	    let (_, active) = catalog::active_schema(&conn)?;
   133	    let mut populations = Vec::new();
   134	    for (name, table) in candidate.visible_tables() {
   135	        let Some(sync) = &table.sync else { continue; };
   136	        let Some(horizon) = &sync.horizon else { continue; };
   137	        let Some(previous) = active.tables.get(name) else { continue; };
   138	        if previous.sync == table.sync || table.ephemeral.is_some() { continue; }
   139	        let threshold = u64::from(horizon.last) * 10;
   140	        if threshold == 0 || threshold > catalog::COUNT_LIMIT { continue; }
   141	        let count = catalog::row_count(&conn, name, threshold)?;
   142	        if count == threshold { populations.push((name.clone(), horizon.last, count)); }
   143	    }
   144	    Ok(populations)
   145	}

   147	/// Strip SQL comments without disturbing quotes, and permit a single trailing
   148	/// terminator. SQLite still parses and authorizes the actual statement.
   149	fn select_body(sql: &str) -> Result<String> {
   150	    if sql.to_ascii_lowercase().contains(PRIVATE) { return Err(("E_SQL_INTERNAL", format!("private inspection views cannot be named in SQL; {CATALOG_HINT}"))); }
   151	    let mut chars = sql.chars().peekable();
   152	    let mut body = String::new();
   153	    let mut ended = false;
   154	    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
   155	        if c == '-' && chars.peek() == Some(&'-') {
   156	            for c in chars.by_ref() { if c == '\n' { break; } }
   157	            body.push('\n');
   158	        } else if c == '/' && chars.peek() == Some(&'*') {
   159	            chars.next();
   160	            while let Some(c) = chars.next() { if c == '*' && chars.peek() == Some(&'/') { chars.next(); break; } }
   161	            body.push(' ');
   162	        } else if c.is_whitespace() { body.push(c); }
   163	        else if ended { return Err(("E_SQL_READ_ONLY", "sql accepts exactly one SELECT statement".into())); }
   164	        else if c == ';' { ended = true; }
   165	        else if matches!(c, '\'' | '"' | '`' | '[') {
   166	            let end = if c == '[' { ']' } else { c };
   167	            body.push(c);
   168	            while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
   169	                body.push(c);
   170	                if c == end {
   171	                    if end != ']' && chars.peek() == Some(&end) { body.push(chars.next().unwrap()); }
   172	                    else { break; }
   173	                }
   174	            }
   175	        } else { body.push(c); }
   176	    }
   177	    let first = body.trim_start().split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_alphabetic()).next().unwrap_or_default();
   178	    if !first.eq_ignore_ascii_case("select") && !first.eq_ignore_ascii_case("with") {
   179	        return Err(("E_SQL_READ_ONLY", "sql accepts one SELECT or WITH … SELECT statement".into()));
   180	    }
   181	    Ok(body)
   182	}
   183	
   184	// A quoted SQL string may itself contain a CLI-looking value. Only flag tokens
   185	// outside SQLite quotes are a misplaced option (including SQLite line comments).
   186	fn misplaced_flag(statement: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
   187	    let mut chars = statement.char_indices().peekable();
   188	    while let Some((offset, c)) = chars.next() {
   189	        if matches!(c, '\'' | '"' | '`' | '[') {
   190	            let end = if c == '[' { ']' } else { c };
   191	            while let Some((_, c)) = chars.next() {
   192	                if c == end {
   193	                    if end != ']' && chars.peek().is_some_and(|(_, c)| *c == end) { chars.next(); }
   194	                    else { break; }
   195	                }
   196	            }
   197	        } else if c == '/' && chars.peek().is_some_and(|(_, c)| *c == '*') {
   198	            chars.next();
   199	            while let Some((_, c)) = chars.next() {
   200	                if c == '*' && chars.peek().is_some_and(|(_, c)| *c == '/') { chars.next(); break; }
   201	            }
   202	        } else if c == '-' {
   203	            for flag in ["--release", "--dormant", "--all-releases", "--limit", "--json-objects", "--json"] {
   204	                if let Some(tail) = statement[offset..].strip_prefix(flag) {
   205	                    if tail.is_empty() || tail.starts_with(char::is_whitespace) || tail.starts_with('=') { return Some(flag); }
   206	                }
   207	            }
   208	        }
   209	    }
   210	    None
   211	}

   213	/// Missing development stores never imply that a neighbouring release is the
   214	/// store to inspect. Name the explicit selection without opening or adopting it.
   215	pub(super) fn store_hint(path: &Path, options: &Options) -> String {
   216	    if options.flags.contains_key("release") || path.exists() { return String::new(); }
   217	    let Some(root) = path.parent().and_then(Path::parent) else { return String::new(); };
   218	    let mut dirs = Vec::new();
   219	    if root.join("store.sqlite").is_file() { dirs.push(root.to_path_buf()); }
   220	    if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(root) {
   221	        for entry in entries.flatten() {
   222	            if entry.file_name() != ".snapback4" && entry.file_type().is_ok_and(|kind| kind.is_dir())
   223	                && entry.path().join("store.sqlite").is_file() { dirs.push(entry.path()); }
   224	        }
   225	    }
   226	    dirs.sort();
   227	    if dirs.is_empty() { return String::new(); }
   228	    format!("; no development store at {}. Deployment stores are present at {}; select one explicitly with --release <dir>",
   229	        path.display(), dirs.iter().map(|dir| dir.display().to_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "))
   230	}

fn refuse(s:impl Into<String>)->RuntimeError {RuntimeError::Structural{code:"E_ADOPT",message:s.into()}}

// Only structural table identifiers change. Literal values, column names,
// operation names and authored defaults are never table identifiers.
fn identifiers(value:&mut serde_json::Value,map:&BTreeMap<String,String>) {
    match value {
        serde_json::Value::Array(xs)=>for x in xs {identifiers(x,map)},
        serde_json::Value::Object(fields)=>for (key,x) in fields {
            if key=="Literal" || key=="defaults" {continue;}
            if matches!(key.as_str(),"table"|"parent") {if let Some(name)=x.as_str().and_then(|s|map.get(s)){*x=serde_json::Value::String(name.clone());continue;}}
            identifiers(x,map);
        },_=>()
    }
}
fn mapped(name:&str,map:&BTreeMap<String,String>)->String {map.get(name).cloned().unwrap_or_else(||name.into())}
fn remap<T:serde::Serialize+serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(value:&T,map:&BTreeMap<String,String>)->Result<T,RuntimeError> {
    let mut json=serde_json::to_value(value).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;identifiers(&mut json,map);
    serde_json::from_value(json).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))
}
pub(crate) fn schema(mut schema:Schema,map:&BTreeMap<String,String>)->Result<Schema,RuntimeError> {
    if map.is_empty(){return Ok(schema)}
    schema.tables=std::mem::take(&mut schema.tables).into_iter().map(|(name,table)|Ok((mapped(&name,map),remap(&table,map)?))).collect::<Result<_,RuntimeError>>()?;
    for m in &mut schema.maintains {*m=remap(m,map)?;m.source=mapped(&m.source,map);m.target=mapped(&m.target,map);}
    for f in &mut schema.backfills {fill(f,map,false)?;}
    for f in &mut schema.downfills {fill(f,map,true)?;}
    for e in &mut schema.extractions {e.child=mapped(&e.child,map);}
    // Remaining table-bearing structural metadata is normalized through the
    // same typed codec; maintains' source/target are handled explicitly above.
    // These maps contain column identifiers, including arbitrary keys such as
    // "parent". Normalize their typed table slots, never their column strings.
    let mut extractions=std::mem::take(&mut schema.extractions);
    for e in &mut extractions {e.parent=mapped(&e.parent,map);}
    let columns=std::mem::take(&mut schema.asset_renames).into_iter().map(|(name,columns)|(mapped(&name,map),columns)).collect();
    schema.table_renames.clear();schema=remap(&schema,map)?;
    schema.extractions=extractions;schema.asset_renames=columns;
    Ok(schema)
}
fn fill(f:&mut crate::schema::backfill::Backfill,map:&BTreeMap<String,String>,down:bool)->Result<(),RuntimeError> {

}

   356	                // declaration on the preceding rollback.  Its archived copy

   358	                // preimage, and the next cycle must issue a fresh receipt so

   404	                // including newer writes and absence since the last restoration.
   405	                let value=fields.get(c).cloned();

   407	            }).collect();
   408	            let e=Evidence{computed:BTreeMap::new(),authored:BTreeSet::new(),reversed,retained:BTreeSet::new(),absent:BTreeSet::new(),epoch:tx.meta("generation")?.and_then(|s|s.parse::<i64>().ok()).unwrap_or(0).saturating_add(1),active:false,inputs,before:BTreeMap::new(),after:patch.clone()};
   409	            tx.conn().execute("INSERT INTO temp._downfill_pending VALUES(?1,?2,?3,?4,?5)",params![t,id,key,canonical_json(&patch),canonical_json(&e)])?;count+=1;Ok(())
   410	        })?;
   411	        if bad.count>0{return Err(refusal(format!("down {} {}: {}",fill.table,fill.name,bad.describe())))}
   412	        if preimages>0 {report.backfills.push(format!("{} {} retained predecessor preimages on {preimages} rows; sample ids [{}]; these rows read stale under the older release until forward; newer source cells remain retained for forward",fill.table,fill.name,preimage_ids.join(", ")));}
   413	        if count>0{report.backfills.push(format!("{} {} projected {count} {} down",fill.table,fill.name,if count==1{"row"}else{"rows"}));}
   414	    }
   415	    Ok(true)
   416	}

   790	pub fn stop_release(options: &Options) -> i32 {
   791	    let result = (|| {
   792	        if crate::store_config::StoreConfig::resolve(options)?.is_some() {
   793	            return Err("E_STORE_UNSUPPORTED: stop is outside the admitted store profile".into());
   794	        }
   795	        let dir = existing_deployment(&directory(options)?)?;
   796	        match crate::release_control::request(&dir, crate::release_control::Command::Stop) {
   797	            Ok(_) => {
   798	                crate::store_owner::wait_released(&dir.join("store.sqlite"), std::time::Duration::from_secs(10))?;
   799	                println!("store stopped: {}", dir.display());
   800	                Ok(())
   801	            }
   802	            Err(control) => match crate::store_owner::wait_released(&dir.join("store.sqlite"), std::time::Duration::ZERO) {
   803	                Ok(()) => {
   804	                    println!("store already stopped: {}", dir.display());
   805	                    Ok(())
   806	                }
   807	                Err(_) => Err(control),
   808	            },
   809	        }
   810	    })();
   811	    match result {
   812	        Ok(()) => 0,
   813	        Err(error) => { eprintln!("stop: {error}"); 1 }
   814	    }
   815	}

   817	pub(crate) fn release_bind(options: &Options) -> Result<std::net::IpAddr, String> {
   818	    let bind = options
   819	        .flags
   820	        .get("bind")
   821	        .map(String::as_str)
   822	        .unwrap_or("127.0.0.1");
   823	    let address: std::net::IpAddr = bind
   824	        .parse()
   825	        .map_err(|_| "--bind must be a literal IPv4 or IPv6 address".to_owned())?;
   826	    if !address.is_loopback() {
   827	        if !options.flags.contains_key("i-understand-cleartext") {
   828	            return Err("non-loopback HTTP sends passwords and bearer tokens in cleartext; use a loopback listener behind a TLS proxy, or explicitly pass --i-understand-cleartext".into());
   829	        }
   830	        eprintln!(
   831	            "WARNING: listening on {address} over CLEARTEXT HTTP. Passwords, bearer tokens, schema and data have no transport protection. Expose only through a TLS proxy on a trusted private hop; see snapback4/README.md."
   832	        );
   833	    }
   834	    Ok(address)
   835	}

    26	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#5-hot-activation-and-ownership — only assignments and committed rebind follow the database commit.
    27	pub(super) fn apply(
    28	    shared: &Shared,
    29	    dir: &std::path::Path,
    30	    command: Command,
    31	) -> Result<Json, String> {
    32	    match command {
    33	        Command::Stop => {
    34	            crate::lifecycle::request_stop();
    35	            Ok(json!({"stopping":true}))
    36	        }
    37	        Command::Status {
    38	            after,
    39	            items_after,
    40	            event,
    41	        } => {

    43	            let mut status=engine.store_mut().release_status(after,items_after.as_deref(),event).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
    44	            status["clock"]=json!({"now":shared.now(),"offsetMs":lock(&shared.clock).offset()});
    45	            Ok(status)
    46	            })
    47	        },
    48	        Command::Prune {
    49	            confirm,

    12	pub(super) fn kinds(sql: &str, schema: &Schema, count: usize, retained: bool) -> Result<Vec<Kind>, String> {
    13	    let mut tables: Tables = schema.visible_tables().map(|(name, table)| {
    14	        let mut columns = vec![("id".into(), Kind::Plain)];
    15	        columns.extend(table.columns.iter().filter(|(name, _)| *name != "id")

    19	    }).collect();
    20	    let statements = Parser::parse_sql(&SQLiteDialect {}, sql).map_err(|e| format!("--json-objects SQL projection: {e}; use --json for SQLite-specific syntax"))?;
    21	    let [Statement::Query(query)] = statements.as_slice() else { return Err("--json-objects takes a SELECT".into()); };
    22	    let columns = query_columns(query, &mut tables)?;
    23	    if columns.len() != count { return Err("--json-objects cannot determine this projection's column types; select explicit columns or use --json".into()); }

    27	fn name(name: &ObjectName) -> Option<String> {
    28	    // SQLite schema qualification bypasses CTE shadowing; do not erase it.
    29	    if name.0.len() != 1 { return None; }
    30	    name.0.last()?.as_ident().map(|id| id.value.to_ascii_lowercase())
    31	}

    33	fn query_columns(query: &Query, inherited: &mut Tables) -> Result<Columns, String> {
    34	    let mut tables = inherited.clone();
    35	    if let Some(with) = &query.with {
    36	        if with.recursive { return Err("--json-objects does not infer recursive CTE types; use --json".into()); }
    37	        for cte in &with.cte_tables {
    38	            if tables.contains_key(&cte.alias.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase()) {
    39	                return Err("--json-objects does not infer shadowing CTEs; use --json".into());
    40	            }
    41	            let mut columns = query_columns(&cte.query, &mut tables)?;
    42	            for (column, alias) in columns.iter_mut().zip(&cte.alias.columns) { column.0 = alias.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase(); }
    43	            tables.insert(cte.alias.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase(), columns);
    44	        }
    45	    }
    46	    set_columns(&query.body, &mut tables)
    47	}

    49	fn relation(factor: &TableFactor, tables: &mut Tables) -> Result<(String, Columns), String> {
    50	    match factor {
    51	        TableFactor::Table { name: object, alias, args: None, .. } => {
    52	            let key = name(object).ok_or("--json-objects does not infer schema-qualified relations; use --json")?;
    53	            let columns = tables.get(&key).ok_or("--json-objects needs application tables or typed CTEs")?.clone();
    54	            Ok((alias.as_ref().map(|a| a.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase()).unwrap_or(key), columns))
    55	        }
    56	        TableFactor::Derived { subquery, alias, .. } => Ok((alias.as_ref().map(|a| a.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase()).unwrap_or_default(), query_columns(subquery, tables)?)),
    57	        _ => Err("--json-objects cannot infer this table expression; use --json".into()),
    58	    }
    59	}

    61	fn set_columns(body: &SetExpr, tables: &mut Tables) -> Result<Columns, String> {
    62	    match body {
    63	        SetExpr::Query(q) => query_columns(q, tables),
    64	        SetExpr::SetOperation { left, right, .. } => {
    65	            let mut left = set_columns(left, tables)?;
    66	            let right = set_columns(right, tables)?;
    67	            if left.len() != right.len() { return Err("incompatible SQL projections".into()); }
    68	            for (l, r) in left.iter_mut().zip(right) { if l.1 != r.1 { l.1 = Kind::Plain; } }
    69	            Ok(left)
    70	        }
    71	        SetExpr::Select(select) => {
    72	            let mut sources = Vec::new();
    73	            for from in &select.from {
    74	                sources.push(relation(&from.relation, tables)?);
    75	                for join in &from.joins { sources.push(relation(&join.relation, tables)?); }
    76	            }
    77	            let mut output = Vec::new();
    78	            for item in &select.projection {
    79	                match item {
    80	                    SelectItem::Wildcard(_) => output.extend(sources.iter().flat_map(|(_, cols)| cols.clone())),
    81	                    SelectItem::QualifiedWildcard(SelectItemQualifiedWildcardKind::ObjectName(object), _) => {
    82	                        let key = name(object).ok_or("unsupported wildcard")?;
    83	                        let (_, cols) = sources.iter().find(|(alias, _)| *alias == key).ok_or("unknown wildcard table")?;
    84	                        output.extend(cols.clone());
    85	                    }
    86	                    SelectItem::UnnamedExpr(expr) => {
    87	                        let mut direct = expr;
    88	                        while let Expr::Nested(inner) = direct { direct = inner; }
    89	                        let label = match direct {
    90	                            Expr::Identifier(id) => id.value.clone(),
    91	                            Expr::CompoundIdentifier(ids) => ids.last().unwrap().value.clone(),
    92	                            _ => expr.to_string(),
    93	                        };
    94	                        output.push((label.to_ascii_lowercase(), kind(expr, &sources)));
    95	                    }
    96	                    SelectItem::ExprWithAlias { expr, alias } => output.push((alias.value.to_ascii_lowercase(), kind(expr, &sources))),
    97	                    _ => return Err("unsupported object-row projection; use --json".into()),
    98	                }
    99	            }
   100	            let mut names = BTreeSet::new();
   101	            if output.iter().any(|(name, _)| !names.insert(name)) {
   102	                return Err("--json-objects needs unique names in every projection; alias duplicate columns".into());
   103	            }
   104	            Ok(output)
   105	        }
   106	        _ => Err("--json-objects needs a SELECT projection; use --json".into()),
   107	    }
   108	}

   110	fn kind(expr: &Expr, sources: &[(String, Columns)]) -> Kind {
   111	    let (table, column) = match expr {
   112	        Expr::Nested(expr) => return kind(expr, sources),
   113	        Expr::Identifier(id) => (None, &id.value),
   114	        Expr::CompoundIdentifier(ids) if ids.len() == 2 => (Some(ids[0].value.to_ascii_lowercase()), &ids[1].value),

In the migrated branch, `deps_same` means BOTH input values and fresh computed
patch equal their saved counterparts. If inputs change but the patch equals
saved `after`, `deps_same` is false: the fresh patch is written when the current
output equals saved `after`, its preimage, or that same fresh patch; any other
manual value refuses. Matching more than one allowed baseline has no precedence
ambiguity: each allows writing the same single fresh patch. Only `deps_same`
plus a still-transformed, present output invokes the parent's explicit preservation
of edited added cells. Every successful staged receipt records fresh inputs and
fresh `after`, retaining the correct predecessor preimages.

If both a native marker and a forward receipt for the same digest are present,
the receipt takes precedence: evaluate the migrated algorithm and its exact
baseline/preimage custody. The marker cannot skip that computation. This overlap
is not produced by ordinary writes (which never create a native marker on a
migrated row), but precedence is explicit for retained/legacy state. Pruned
membership is checked first and cannot become native acceptance. Down receipts
have distinct down digests and do not establish native-forward status.

“Affected” for bridge listing includes domain-loosened tables, retained new
authoritative tables, and identities whose table/asset-column spelling moves.
Use the target spelling for a renamed identity, with its current spelling noted
as provenance; never list the aliases as two independent tables. Emit direct
lowered Quarry readers/writers on those tables. The separate manual audit still
covers indirect rule/action/worker/UI dependencies.

## 9. Edited migrated outputs (ROLL)

Commissioned for 0.4.39, 2026-10-22. LLP 3000.000.000 §20 and its review
clarifications govern default rollback views and the closed safety boundary.
An in-place output edited under its declaring source may use a declared down
on its current assembled image, or keep the exact value in a target domain
which already admits it. A failing old type/constraint still refuses; no
per-row widening or invented scalar is allowed. Unedited outputs keep exact
preimage precedence, with a receipt saying when that old view is stale until
forward. Real forward conflicts include competing values and bridge repair.

Receipts distinguish the original preimage, authored newer image, saved
computation, selected old physical image and presence. Equal explicit inputs
alone cannot authorize retaining an edited output: fresh point/existence
recomputation must also agree with the saved computation, or exactly equal
the actual authored image. Changed projected cells, parents, pruned evidence
and meter cuts still refuse atomically. Editing never creates native-birth
status. Format 9 fences this retained law, including after selecting old source;
format 8 remains readable and upgrades transactionally on successful adoption.
Repeated cycles, partially retired outputs and table-name changes preserve
that evidence. The implementation adds focused regressions for those paths.


## 10. Wave-25 day-two friction (DX8)

Implementer: Codex / Charlie Cheever, 2026-10-23. Commission: wave-25 fix list
8b #1–#13, building on DX7 and Integration 23/24. This amendment is a reviewed
implementation commission, not author acceptance or a publication claim.
The no-JavaScript migration, atomic activation, job-meter and row-lifetime
custody laws above still apply. Integration 23 owns rollback-view selection and
its trigger; SEC9 owns column-write authority, security gates and adversarial
campaign reach. DX8 changes neither of those lanes' policy.

### Migration interpretation and current-value renames

Backfill arguments and lookups read the assembled pre-patch snapshot, before
any simultaneous rename/backfill writes outputs. Historical argument names
therefore name predecessor fields. A declaration's immutable meaning is its
normalized typed-IR digest. Every changed-meaning refusal, both continuously
carried and after a historical gap, prints old and new full digests. A new name
is a new declaration; pruning does not reset names or immutable definitions.
Prune previews name known down projections whose native/reverse or overlapping
forward-preimages they discard. This warning is privileged operator output;
prune remains explicit and destructive, and unavailable evidence still refuses
subsequent reversal/re-entry. Preview never mutates live history.

For the generated `$rename:down` with identical declared old/new scalar types,
the current renamed cell outranks its non-null retained predecessor cell. This
is an identity spelling change, not a historical computation: v1 must see the
edited v2 quote, not the original quote. Stage it on the existing newer snapshot
and preserve native/reverse evidence in the same transaction. Repeated
rollback/forward cycles retain that current value. Different-type renames still
refuse even when sample values happen to fit. Authored down projections retain
their exact forward-preimage/non-null-native precedence; a generated rename
does not grant another declaration permission to replace protected cells.
Conflicting edits under an older view still require an explicit bridge where
existing receipt custody cannot reconcile them. The change stays isolated in
backfills.rs; it does not alter rollback views or release bridges.

### One child per list element

`extract CHILD from PARENT via REF each: {destination:sourceList}` extends the
existing one-child extraction. Exactly one mapped destination is a required
scalar image/file/video; its historical source is a bounded list with an
identical element type (optionally a nullable whole list). Other mapped fields
retain the existing immutable authoritative scalar-copy law. Empty lists create
zero children. A null whole list remains null after an unchanged empty cycle;
a populated child set becomes a real list. Duplicate asset elements refuse:
one asset cannot acquire two child homes. Unsupported types refuse, never copy
or reupload bytes. Default `extract` keeps its existing whole-cell behavior.

Per-parent element receipts bind current asset IDs to stable child lifetimes
and ordinal positions; new historical elements get deterministic child IDs,
independent destination history refuses. Current child asset edits keep their
child ID. Reverse selection gathers every extant child, including native v2
children with valid captured parent-lifetime evidence, preserving receipt order
and appending native children in ID order. It moves current homes back into the
old list and records the current element-to-child map. Returning forward follows
that map, so old-client reordering preserves child identity and appending a new
asset creates one new child. Removed elements mark their receipt-owned child asset absent (an internal null),
leaving the retained child outside the active population under ordinary narrowing; they do not
silently regain an asset or get deleted. A target list that cannot represent
the full current population follows ordinary narrowing, never truncates it.
Every receipt-owned child and its parent-lifetime evidence is validated before
either forward or reverse processing, including removed elements and intact
dormant nulls. A missing/pruned receipt-owned child or invalid parent lifetime refuses rather
than recreating history or recapturing a reused parent ID. Reverse selection
refuses atomically if a populated child asset home remains in narrowed storage;
it names the retained population and requires a loosened child-domain bridge
that restores those rows before selecting old source. Migration-owned null
removals have no live child asset home and stay dormant across repeated cycles.

A successfully applied element extraction records durable definition custody,
including an empty initial population. Temporarily retiring its child table or
declaration suspends that law when the selected parent no longer declares the
source list. Re-entry with the same definition resumes current child rows and
homes rather than demanding or replaying the consumed list. It validates every
receipt and every restored/current child's existing parent lifetime, captured
authority, immutable scalar copies, ledger home and bytes; it never retroactively
captures independent children born while the declaration was absent. Missing
source plus unknown definition refuses. New parents created while the child
table is retired can have zero children. Ordinary narrowed storage remains
retained; no row or home is synthesized. Resuming, as every activation, is atomic
and metered with the child page and parent image sharing its job allowance.

Source/destination read authority and column gates retain the existing strict
extraction checks in both directions, including captured parent-authority agreement. One extraction owns each child table, avoiding competing sources for native children. No user migration endpoint or broader
asset audience is introduced. Forward, reverse and resumed traversal share the
activation page's job meter with every child decode and retained scratch image.
The still-resident serialized page and accumulated children consume one allowance;
length preflight reserves before fetching/decoding, and only dropped scratch is
released. Per-parent traversal/allocation/writes use job meters; a cut aborts the
entire activation. Home transfers, row changes,
receipts, ordinary reference/narrowing/uniqueness/cap validation and generation
publication share the existing writer transaction. Successful adoption fences
this law with release-store format 10, including after selecting old source;
formats 8/9 remain readable and failed adoption does not upgrade their marker.
No successful later adoption downgrades the marker. Serialized schemas carrying
`each` also require `release-child-extraction-each-v1`, so older engines refuse
the new interpretation before accepting a compiled schema.

### Operator processes, development clock and real accounts

`snapback4 stop <deployment-dir>` uses the existing same-owner authenticated
local release-control channel, then awaits the kernel lock-release barrier.
Already stopped is success. An unverifiable/live foreign owner refuses: never
unlink a lock or signal a guessed PID. Proof hosts/frontends/tool commands own
an explicit process group, including npm wrappers and children. Stop, failure
and parent exit release that entire owned group through live keeper/pipe
custody; cleanup is bounded and cannot silently leave a serving descendant.
Frontend keeper-backed groups are registered for group-drain checks too. If a
keeper is lost while a member survives, stop/startup cleanup must report an
explicit bounded cleanup failure, even when the host handle has already exited.
Processes deliberately leaving custody are outside that promise. Scripts whose
stdout is one JSON line use `npm run --silent`; logs remain separate.
Changelog/help qualification treats `run` immediately following npm/bun/pnpm
as that package manager’s subcommand; later explicit Snapback invocations
on the same line still advertise flags and remain checked.

A password-authenticated development host exposes clock status/advance with
fixture/persona doors closed. It requires an exact full `service:operator`
bearer token minted through the existing local store authority. Ordinary users,
other seats, read-scoped sessions, unauthenticated requests and production
hosts cannot use it. Staging keeps its existing full-service-seat authorization;
explicit unsafe development and guest-schema development retain their existing local fixture behavior.
Authenticated development jumps preserve live full/read session families and
worker leases by default in the same store transaction as the jump's durable
authority effects; expired/revoked families never revive. Explicit
`sessions: 'expire'` requests expiry testing. Header/SDK reconciliation keeps
current clients alive across the jump. The development offset is process-local
and returns to wall time on restart; staging retains DX7's persistent checkpoint
and paused-drain behavior. A failed/ambiguous jump is never automatically
replayed. `startDev` exposes operator-backed now/advance/drain without opening
fixture doors. Production uses wall time and refuses clock control.

`provisionAccounts` shares seedAccounts plan validation, generated credentials,
identity retry/deadline behavior, result shape, selected seat and provision
mutation. It accepts production through real signup/login and
ordinary authorized mutations; it refuses development and uses no seed/system
bypass; staging continues to use seedAccounts. Custom per-user args retain seedAccounts' existing merge precedence.
A minted service seat is only that exact principal, not a superuser. The served schema exposes `service_identities`, a list of explicit positive
viewer/service equality facts and declared route/schedule seats, excluding result
and enum literals. Both local CLI minting (live or stopped) and the production
helper warn on stderr when a seat has no matching explicit authorization identity.
This is conservative diagnostic evidence, never a proof of admission or denial;
public rules and dynamic application roles still decide actual authority. The mutation's actual read and write rules decide.

### Inspection and saved artifacts

Default active sql/data/releases announce the retained dormant row count when
nonzero. Missing active-table errors identify a retained table and its row count
and name a concrete dormant inspection command. Inspection remains a privileged
read-only consistent snapshot, outside application rules. Only direct,
schema-proven media cells in `sql --json-objects` decode to their ordinary wire
JSON values; positional `--json` remains compatible. Truncation and dormancy
notices go to stderr, preserving JSON stdout; existing limit/more fields stay.

An identical-source deploy with --save-version can refresh an existing saved
version only if the complete Quarry source set and exact bytes match. Differing
source refuses. Generated client artifacts are emitted from that saved source's
Bound, independently of the working tree; fixtures/source evidence stay intact.
Refresh follows successful adoption/no-op and records the correct retained
release identity. Replaying an old source never silently emits the current API.

### Paging, proof assertions and contract advice

Board/roster starters and list recipes use newest-first `last N by .id`, while
explicit oldest-first examples remain labelled. The language's ordering default
does not change. Cursors are opaque evaluator-issued positions: send next back
unchanged; a row id/projection is not a cursor. `exhaustPages(readPage)` begins
with null, gathers array pages, follows next, and refuses denial/loading,
malformed/repeated cursors or its explicit page bound. It never turns a capped
or partial read into complete evidence. Projections change fields, not cursor
meaning/order/completeness.

Day-two recipes compare by stable id across stages and declared common fields,
not list position or whole differently-shaped row images. IDs created by a
frozen v1-client replay are recorded and excluded from preservation baselines.
V2-native IDs may be absent from an exact v1 view; they must reappear unchanged
on forward. Domain-specific synthesized old values need an authored projection
assertion, not an equality claim for incompatible representations.

renderedText(..., null) equals omitted options. Whitespace normalization,
case-sensitive exact matching by default, explicit substring matching and DX7's
legal scroll reachability remain unchanged. The lane-031 full-line regression
must match mounted reachable `Pump logged.` text, without widening hidden clips.
Write-authority hints explain that a mutation require and the caller's table
rule are separate gates. The captured-vs-live-parent card describes existing
lifetime/audience semantics; it grants no new authority.

Old-client INPUT BREAK advice follows accepted wire identities, including
references through declared table renames and lowered aliases/defaults. Real
removed/required/narrowed inputs still warn. Pure object-result field additions
are RESULT NOTE, not RESULT REVIEW or an adoption hazard; changed/removed fields
and domains retain review. These remain conservative advice, not a proof of
unchanged business behavior. No runtime input validation is weakened.
